body: Close to Jungle Beach or an easy 30min walk from Unawatuna Beach, the Japanese Peace Pagoda is a simple but must-see Pagoda in Unawatuna. If you get a chance to chat with the resident monk Rev Asami, I highly recommend! He is so nice, thoughtful, and proud of the pagoda (which he initiated and built over 25 years ago). The purpose of the pagoda is enriching and I really wish there was more information posted around to explain it to tourists, it’s more than just Buddha statues - it symbolizes peace, respect, and love. There is also a nice statue on the main grass level near the back to commemorate the lives lost during the 2004 tsunami. I HIGHLY recommend it for sunset (see pics in the review), it was beautiful how the light hits the pagoda - golden hour on the golden statues - and very peaceful atmosphere overall. You can also participate in the meditative/chanting service and drum along with the local monks around sunset. It’s only 15mins and a great cultural experience.
title: Perfect spot for sunset!

It is such a peaceful Place and so beautiful Buddhist temple In Sri Lanka. It is a really restful, peaceful spot. There is breathtaking view of Galle fort and Indian Ocean from the temple. It is a bit out of the way to walk there from the main road. It wasn't crowded and Kept very clean. We came her to watch the sunset and its perfect. An absolute must! body: The Japanese Peace Pagoda stands prominently on a small hill overlooking the ocean. Painted brilliant white, it is highly visible for miles. This beautiful structure was built by Japanese Buddhist monks in 2005, paid for by the people of Japan and opened to the public by President Rajapaksa. It was built as a peace temple for the people of Sri Lanka at a time when the civil war was raging. It also commemorates the loss of 16 Japanese students at Yala in the 2004 tsunami. There is no doubt that it is a peaceful place to walk around and provides a good view of the ocean and glorious sunset. There is a little sign warning you to remove your shoes, not to eat or smoke nor to use your mobile phone. There is a Buddhist shrine next to the pagoda and you are allowed in if appropriately dressed. It is free to enter but donations are expected.

body: The so-called Peace Pagoda is a nice place for a short trip outside Galle. Of course you can take a taxi or Tuk-Tuk but it’s also possible to reach it by bicycle. Just take the main road leading to the east along the coast to Unawatuna. After leaving the city of Galle you will pass after a while some traffic lights. On the left side there’s a cement factory. Just pass the small bridge crossing a river and then turn right and follow the street going up the hill. It will lead you to the Peace Pagoda (on the way going there you’ll pass the path to the Jungle Beach). Don’t expect a large complex like a monastery. There just the “Pagoda” which is a large white dagoba and a building aside with the prayer room and some Buddha statues inside. The monks are very friendly and will invite you to go inside.I recommend that you go there for sunset. The sky looks beautiful with the white dagoba in the front (nice photos!). And it’s not as hot as during the day anymore which makes it less exhausting to go up the hill. Or you combine it with a longer stay at the Jungle Beach.

body: Three of us walked to the Pagoda from Pokhara, and back. The trail is uphill to the pagoda and takes a few hours. There have been reports of muggings in the past and it is probably safest to go after 9 am when there are more people around, and walk in a group. We did not feel any apprehension today. Once you cross the suspension bridge below which locals do their washing, clean themselves and swim, you turn right up some steps, then turn left on a path passing fields on your left and with a high fence on your right until you can find the trail through a wide gate in the fence. On the return hike we saw many monkeys. This walk back is much quicker.The pagoda itself is interesting and there are enough English signs to get an idea of what the place is about. There are quite a fewer restaurants to relax in and enjoy the beautiful view of lake Fewa ( Phewa Tal) and Pokhara city.Rather than hiking back you can, alternatively, choose to walk down to the lake to get a boat back to lakeside or take a taxi .This activity is a nice day out with exercise and rewarding views.

body: The Peace Pagoda lives up to its name. The huge white pagoda seems to radiate serenity as soon as you approach. Climb around it and see the beautiful views over the ocean and to Galle in the distance. There are different "altars" around the pagoda with explanations about the Buddha underneath. Beside the pagoda is a small temple which you can enter. On the same site is the granite memorial to the tsunami victims and also a statue of a "monkey man". body: We walked to the Japenese Peace Pagoda from Galle Fort, mainly along the coast and then up a hill through a small forest. We also saw people travelling up to the pagoda in tuktuks, so this is also an option if you don't fancy walking in the hot sun, or have limited time.The pagoda is so peaceful, there were only a couple of other visitors while we were there and it was lovely to rest for 15-20 minutes and take in the views of Galle. The setting is beautiful, providing the perfect place to read, write or just have a few minutes to sit and daydream.There is a dress code (your legs must be covered to the knee) but sarongs are provided so don't worry if you are wearing shorts. body: This is a quiet place where you can appreciate human dedication to Buddhism and peace. It is built at very spacial location. On the day I visited, I whole place for myself until I left. Absolutely fantastic! Do not miss Hanuman shrine, it is popular with locals, tooRumassala is the name of the area where Pagoda is erected. According to Ramayana, it is where Princess Sita (daughter of Mother Earth and avatar of Godess Laksmi) was imprisoned by demon King Ravana. In a battle to free her Lakshman, her brother in law, was badly wounded and Hanuman went to Himalayas to fetch medicinal herbs to heal him. Unable to recognize the herbs, Hanuman brought the whole mountain. But in the process a large chunk of it fell and formed Rumassala Hill. Medicinal plants are still growing in that area and the name Unawatuna is derived from "onna vetuna" meaning "here it fell".On the other hand, famous sci-fi writer, Arthur Clarke suggested it was a meteorite strike which still causes magnetic disturbance in the area.Great place to be silent and to be inspired
title: Great place to be silent

Then you have to get down near road to Rumassala and travel by tuk tuk about 10 min uphill passing jungle beach. body: AccessYou can take a tuk-tuk all the way to the pagoda. It's definitely worth it if you can't handle heat very well. Otherwise, you can walk up there either the way that Google maps suggest or you can take a shorter route. Mind that the shorter route is for fit people as it's high, slippery rocks going up & down in the jungle.So, from the Unawatuna beach, go west on the Yaddehimulla Rd. all the way to South Ceylon Hillside hotel (guest house?), then continue straight on what looks like a path on Google maps. The area is free from tourists, shops, only locals live there. But it's safe. The road will end at some hut, you're on the right way. Keep going, follow the path on rocks going up & down. At some point there will be a kind of intersection where 1 path will go down & left - that's going to the Jungle beach, and another one up & to the right - that's towards the Peace Pagoda. You're not going to be lost from there.PlaceYou need to remove your shoes & cover your shoulders & knees. They provide kerchiefs if you don't have anything covering you. Entrance is free, however, the guy there lets youinside a temple building & asks for a donation upfront. Also, this guy got some balls - we had a 20Rs & 5000Rs, so I gave him a 20. He asked if I had a hundred. :-DYou are allowed to take pictures in the place but still be respectful - try to stay quiet, not turn your back on statues of Lord Buddha & do not make obnoxious or disrespectful photos/comments. The place is interesting but other than a few shots & enjoying the atmosphere for a bit, there's nothing to do there & the heat is killing. InfrastructureThere's a toilet (hole in the wall, no soap), there's no shops there (have your water in good supply), there's few tuk-tuks there happy to get you back to Unawatuna. They started with 500Rs to Unawatuna beach, we talked them down to 300Rs. See what you can do. :-)

body: We dropped in at the peace pagoda in early July and spent a couple of hours there. The pagoda itself is of very recent origin, a gift from the Japanese. Its a strikingly white structure standing in stark relief to the great views of Galle Bay and the Indian Ocean. We unfortunately timed our visit around noon. It is hot and if you are planning to walk around the pagoda, please remember that is is a shoes-off barefoot zone and not the most pleasant experience in the baking sun. Late evening is probably a much better time and also affords great views of the sunset.Rumassala hill, on which the pagoda is built has a more hoary tradition since it is believed to be a broken chunk of the himalayan peak carried by the monkey god Hanuman during the great battle between Rama and Ravana (as retold in the great Indian epic Ramayana). There is indeed a nice little temple to the left of the pagoda with a tall statue of Hanuman and even more interestingly, a rare statue of Ravana himself. Worth spending a couple of hours taking in the views and soaking some nice history/mythology of the place

body: The Japanese Peace Pagoda is a bit from from the Unawatuna beach and from Galle, but easily accessible by tuk tuk. We hired a tuk tuk on our way back from Unawatuna Beach to Galle, and we asked the driver to wait for us (which was a great idea as there were no tuk tuks available anywhere nearby in the evening and we would have been stuck). We watched the sun set and sat looking up at the pagoda for a very long time. A very soothing experience.
title: Absolutely stunning

body: If you are staying in Galle, then this is a 20-25 minute drive and its very close by from the Unawatuna beach.This place is so peaceful, its so quiet and beautiful!... The view from the pagoda (view of the lighthouse) is just superb!Clear blue skies, and the blue sea - you will not want to leave this place! Please remember to wear full length clothes (legs covered) or carry a shawl with you to cover your legs when you enter this place.
title: Must visit! Do not miss this!

body: Close to jungle beach. Awesome place to take a picture of Galle Fort. Need to take off your shoes and cover you legs if you are wearing shorts.
title: Fabulouse view, beautiful temple!

body: The view is ok but too busy area for us, it is a pity to waste time here if you are on a trip with just few days
title: nothing interesting

body: peaceful...and in the middle of the woods on a hilltop...a must do if you are in Unawatuna...additionally, the jungle beach is down the hill from the pagoda...again, a must do place if you have come all the way to catch a glimpse of the pagoda!
title: bliss!

body: The beautiful white building boasts a spectacular view, and definitely exudes a calming presence. The tiny road to reach it is a bit tedious, but worth it if you're looking for something off the beaten track. Car is easy enough. Walking may take some time. bring your own water if you walk. there are no refreshment stalls up there.
title: Unexpectedly enjoyable

body: The Japanese Peace temple is a very relaxing point situated near the ocean. It's a one time visit. Would had been better if there was someone around the temple to show and tell us more about the place.
title: Calm Refreshing Experience

body: This is so beautiful, so peaceful , when you go there the feeling you get is ,i cant describe in words!!! amazing place for Buddhist people and people who love cultural places !!!
title: Beautiful Place

body: This is a Buddhist temple. It is called the Japanese Peace Pagoda since it was a gift from the government of Japan to the people of Sri Lanka.Be there at 6 PM if you wish to see / participate in the drumming / meditation session, as well as to see the sunset.
title: Nice and interesting

body: Beautiful and quiet place. Great views! It's a couple of minutes walk from Jungle Beach. Few tuk-tuks waiting there. Do not pay more than 350 to get to Unawatuna :)
title: Beautiful

body: Excellent place to watch sun set over the ocean. Come after a day at the jungle beach with your loved one and enjoy a romantic sunset together :)
title: Beautiful sunset

body: If you're staying in the area, don't miss out on the peace pagoda! Rent a scooter or get yourself dropped off by tuk tuk. Go during sunset (17:30 - 18:00) and meet the Japanese priest if he is around!
title: Awesome view

body: We went here before going to the jungle beach nearby. It's a nice stop. Very well recommended also for a family with children like we have.
title: Very nice Pagoda

body: its good place to visit, its on the way to jungle beach, good all statues of buddha kept their and his life cycle explained very nicely.one more interesting sri hanuman statue is located at this place, one monk told us whole the story of hanuman rescued laxman with medicines of Himalaya and that Himalaya's part fall down from his hand and it's named as 'unawatuna'.... must visit
title: peaceful, quite, well maintained

body: We went in the afternoon but the location of this place is such that you can see the beach from this temple and when the weather is not hot , cool breeze is blowing. It was so peaceful that i wanted to just sit down and meditate or go to sleep there. Its a must visit especially when the sun is not out.There is a hanuman statue nearby.Way to the jungle beach area is also nearby.
title: Very peaceful

body: We went to this temple as part of a guided tour organised by our hotel. It's a peaceful (no pun intended) place. You get to see a beautiful landscape view of Galle forte from afar.
title: Peaceful, try make it to the drumming ritual!

body: When in south of Sri Lanka I always have to come here. A beautiful building at the ocean panorama. The place is really peaceful. Join in on the ceremony led by the resident monk and experience the place not just like a sight.
title: Peaceful panoramic view

body: Great spot to watch the sunset! It's not a low structure (positioned along the edge of a drop-off). It's peaceful and tranquil.
title: Beautiful view of the rocks and ocean

body: This is a very nice place with very kind people. It's worth visiting at sunset because it is a nicest than.
title: Very nice place

body: It's a nice and quiet place in Unawatuna, neareby you can see one under stones remple with one old monk very antix temple
title: Nice and big Pagoda

body: as the name says, this pagoda does have a very peacefull atmosphere to it. especially after long road trips from bentota we needed the relaxing moments and found them here!
title: peacefull

body: We walked all the way there from our hotel and it was a very nice walk with a lot of nice views. We liked everything we seen and it was definitely worth going there. Such nice people.
title: Great place

body: Peace pagoda is located inside the jungle beach - roomaswala. On the way to jungle beach ypu can cover this attraction.
title: Peaceful location

body: Unfortunately it was a quick drop by for only 10 mins or so. What a beautiful and tranquil place. The architecture is amazing and gold Buddha breathtaking. I loved the memorial to the tsunami , i was fortunate enough to witness a family come and pay their respects that day too. It's a must visit if you are in the area
title: Stunningly beautiful

body: Peaceful place, invites to meditation. Very clean and breathtaking. Nice words about Buddhas history and life, wisdom and teachings. Beautiful sculptures! I love it! Don't miss it!
title: Great experience!!!

body: Great views and very peaceful. Nice explanatory / historical placards under the different Buddha statues. Worth a short visit to appreciate the tranquility and unlike other temples, you don't feel forced to leave a "donation".
title: Quiet and peaceful

body: Excellent view from top.... very peaceful. Also, the paintings around the pagoda are beautiful and gives you information on Buddha life event
title: Excellent view from top

body: A beautiful Buddhist temple with a great view of the beaches and Galle Fort. Definitely worth a stop in on your way through to Jungle Beach.
title: Peace Pagoda

body: Very good locations to spend evenings and to watch the sunset. Panoramic views from this location is excellent.
title: Excellent Sunset Views

body: This is called Japanese Peace Pagoda, because it was built by Japanese Mahayana Buddhist priests of a Japanese Organization~Japanese Nipponzan-Myōhōji order, who has built other Pagodas in Amparai and Siri Pada. It is not in Japanese architectural style and is like any other Stupa or Dagoba in Buddhist temples all over the country.
title: Not in Japanese style.

body: Beautiful & peaceful. Wonderful view of the beach. A must visit having a calming effect on the mind and soul.
title: Peaceful...
Great views of the ocean and Galle Harbor
body: Great View of Galle Harbor and the ocean from up on the hill. Al;so very close to the two "Jungle Beaches" so its a good stop off after a day at the beach.

title: Sunset visit at a beautiful peaceful place.
body: I visited this place around sunset. Its amazing view is stunning. You can visit it any any time. It's quiet and peaceful. Also you can attend a service by the monk in the morning if you wish. No entry fee. Donations are always welcome.

title: Nice surrounds - temple not particularly impressive
body: Not really worth a special visit but it's nice walking around the area if you happen to be passing through.

title: Be separated from crowded world
body: Japanese pagoda is situated near the jungle beach "Roomassala" near to unawatuna beach. As this is situated near the beach but away from the city area visiting this place will help you to relax your mind and enjoy the beauty of the sun setting and the wonderful coastal area. This will also provide you a full view of galle city and unawatuna beach near by. But please keep in mind to wear properly as this is a religious place . Be kind enough not to enter the temple with beach dresses. Enjoy the wonderful scenic place

title: Peaceful
body: We were alone at this peaceful Buddhist shrine offering stunning views of Galle including the fort, the lighthouse and the church. Definitely worth a visit

title: A lovely scenic place to visit
body: Lovely place to visit with excellent views, completely free although contributions and donations are accepted, as they would be at a mosque, church or temple.

title: highly recommended
body: this was truly amazing experience, i liked it a lot. there were no tourist while we visited, it has special atmosphere in the evening, its serene,clean and views are stunning.

title: Beautiful location and view
body: Amazing views. Peaceful place. Beautiful gold figurines go Buddha, describing different stages in his life. Educational.

title: Beautiful View
body: It was a bit of a climb for our van to get up to this spot. It's very near jungle beach and overlooks galle and the beach. Very scenic view esp if you climb up the pagoda. You would have to take off your shoes first before you enter.It's a 10-20 min visit since there's really nothing much to see except enjoy the view.You can visit if you have time, but this doesn't need to be prioritized.

title: Peace Buddist temple
body: Took a tuk tuk from fort for Rs 600 (Return included)It is uphill on the mountain and must visit for buddhist preachers. In evening, you can see the skyline of Galle city from the monument which was quite serene. Other attraction near it is Jungle beach.
